name: Breech Presentation, External Cephalic Version and Malpositions

reference.source: Sakshi Arora Obstetrics 9th Edition / RCOG Green-top Guideline on Breech Management
clinicalPearls: Frank breech extended legs is the most common breech type (65-70%) and safest for vaginal delivery
Footling breech carries the highest risk of umbilical cord prolapse due to poor lower segment fill
External cephalic version is offered at thirty-six to thirty-seven weeks gestation, successful in fifty percent
Lovset maneuver rotates the fetal trunk one hundred eighty degrees to deliver extended arms under the pubic arch
Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit maneuver flexes and delivers the aftercoming fetal head using jaw traction
reference.pathophysiology: Breech presentation occurs when the fetal buttocks or lower extremities enter the maternal pelvic inlet. While present in up to twenty percent of pregnancies at twenty-eight weeks, over ninety percent spontaneously cephalize by thirty-six weeks as the heavier, larger fetal head accommodates the wider fundus. Persistent breech presentation associates with prematurity, uterine anomalies, placental location (previa), polyhydramnios, and multiple gestations.
additionalDifferentials: Frank breech versus complete versus footling breech
additionalInvestigations: Obstetric ultrasound confirming fetal lie, presentation, estimated fetal weight and attitude of head
Pelvic examination during labor to assess cervical dilatation, station and exclude cord prolapse
